# Native adapter evidence

Checked 2026-10-27. Tests use only local files and processes, with no agent credentials or network.

- `codex-pretooluse.json` is the recorded codex-cli 0.164 payload supplied with the contract. Only `cwd` changed, to `/project`; session and tool metadata remain intact. Source: the contract's `codex-pretooluse-sample.json` scratchpad artifact. [Codex hooks](https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks/) documents the compatible deny output and exit 2 behavior. For secret writes, tests derive documented `apply_patch` payloads with patch text in `tool_input.command`; `Edit|Write` are only matcher aliases.
- `cursor-pretooluse.json` is a representative payload transcribed from [Cursor's common schema and preToolUse reference](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks#pretooluse), with neutral identifiers. It is documentation evidence, not a live recording. The adapter must translate `Shell` and Cursor's permission response.
- `opencode-before.json` records the documented `tool.execute.before` callback shape from [OpenCode plugins](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/). It is documentation evidence, not a live recording. `run-opencode.mjs` supplies the real Bun shell and project paths to local plugin exports; it never executes the requested tool. SDK/network client use is outside this offline boundary. The lifecycle mode also sends `tool.execute.after`, `file.edited` and `session.idle`, letting the test observe lint and format effects through an executable local ruff fixture.
- `claude-plugin.schema.json` transcribes the metadata and skill-path portion of [Claude Code's plugin manifest schema](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference). That page documents the schema as field tables, not a downloadable JSON Schema; this fixture says explicitly which subset it records. Runtime checks additionally enforce root containment, existence, version parity and skill-content parity, accepting both a skill folder and a parent directory of skill folders. The package is private and has no pack/files/bin configuration, so a future release test must check the actual tarball.

Reference fixtures are built in real temporary registries by `validate-native-adapters.test.ts`: [Codex TOML](https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-advanced/), [OpenCode JSON/JSONC](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/), [permissions](https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/), [formatter command arrays](https://opencode.ai/docs/formatters/), and [Cursor hooks](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks). The fixtures never run their declared commands.
